# CBDB-Desktop: Networks form revisions, 2026-10-08

Found while testing the Networks form for the user's guide, not from an automated-testing report, so these entries have no CBDB-D numbers yet. Assign numbers as needed. All three changes are in Code/networks_form_query.go. They were compiled and checked against test queries using the Law Entry seed list (11 Song persons, LawEntryPeopleSongIDs.txt).

## Summary

| Ref | Issue | Fix | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| NET-1 | Kin edges were copied into ZZ_SN_NETWORK with no edge distance | sqlCopyKin now copies ZZ_NETWORK_LIST.c_distance into c_edge_dist | Compiled, tested |
| NET-2 | The aggregate record count skipped kin edges, so single-kin pairs got no link description and mixed pairs were mislabelled | sqlInsertAgg counts rows with Count(\*) instead of Count(c_edge_dist) | Compiled, tested |
| NET-3 | Edge distance was one short for every edge that reached a newly found person | After the loop, c_distance is recomputed as the larger of the two endpoints' node distances | Compiled, tested |

## NET-1: Kin edges had no edge distance

**Symptom.** In the results export, every kin edge showed EdgeDist = 0. In the first test, all 98 kin rows had 0.

**Cause.** sqlCopyNonkin copies ZZ_NETWORK_LIST.c_distance into ZZ_SN_NETWORK.c_edge_dist. sqlCopyKin left that column out, so it was NULL for every kin edge. The exports turn that NULL into 0.

**Fix.** c_edge_dist was added to sqlCopyKin's column list, and ZZ_NETWORK_LIST.c_distance to its SELECT. This matches the non-kin copy.

**Other effects.** Before the fix, the UCINet and GUESS exports gave every kin tie a distance of 0, so every kin tie was drawn in the distance-1 colour.

## NET-2: Kin ties missing from the aggregate record count

**Symptom.** In the aggregated-relations table, a pair of people with exactly one kin tie had a blank link description. Non-kin pairs were labelled correctly: "N: …" for a single tie, and "Multiple associations merged" for several.

**Cause.** buildAggregate Step 2 set c_rec_count with Count(ZZ_SN_NETWORK.c_edge_dist). COUNT(column) skips NULLs, and because of NET-1 every kin edge had a NULL distance. So kin edges added nothing to the count:

- **One kin tie:** count 0. Step 3 (= 1) and Step 4 (&gt; 1) both skipped the row, so its label stayed blank. The first test had 80 such pairs.
- **Two or more kin ties:** also count 0, also blank (3 pairs).
- **One association plus one kin tie:** count 1. Step 3 then gave a merged pair a single-tie label, taken from whichever row SQLite happened to return first (3 pairs).
- **Several associations plus one kin tie:** undercounted, but still labelled "Multiple associations merged" (12 pairs).

**Fix.** Step 2 now uses Count(\*) AS c_rec_count. This counts merged edges directly and no longer depends on any column being non-NULL. NET-1 alone would have fixed the symptom. This change keeps it fixed if a NULL distance ever appears again.

**Note on the Access version.** Access's Count([field]) also skips NULLs. If the VBA kin copy (tQueryCopyKinStr) also leaves out the distance, the Access version has the same problem.

## NET-3: Edge distance one short for edges that reach a new person

**Symptom.** With maximum node distance = 1, all 7 edges had EdgeDist = 0. Each one ran from a seed (node distance 0) to a newly found person (node distance 1). With maximum distance = 2, edges from a distance-1 person to a newly found distance-2 person were labelled 1.

**Intended rule.** Edge distance should be the larger of the two endpoints' node distances. Seed–seed = 0, seed–first-round = 1, first-round–first-round = 1, and so on.

**Cause.** sqlSelectNonkin and sqlSelectKin set ZZ_NETWORK_LIST.c_distance to ZZ_SP_NETWORK.c_node_dist of the **source** person. When an edge is inserted, the node's own distance isn't known yet, because new people are added to ZZ_SP_NETWORK only by expandPeopleList at the end of each pass. Nothing went back afterwards to correct c_distance, since sqlNodeDistUpdate fills only c_node_dist. Edges in the closing pass, between two people already in the list, happened to come out right. Every edge that found a new person was one short.

**Fix.** A new constant, sqlEdgeDistUpdate, runs as the first step of finalizeResults, before copyToSocialNetwork. At that point every endpoint has its final node distance.

UPDATE ZZ_NETWORK_LIST SET c_distance = MAX(

COALESCE((SELECT sp.c_node_dist FROM ZZ_SP_NETWORK sp WHERE sp.c_person_id = ZZ_NETWORK_LIST.c_personid), 0),

COALESCE((SELECT sp.c_node_dist FROM ZZ_SP_NETWORK sp WHERE sp.c_person_id = ZZ_NETWORK_LIST.c_node_id), 0))

Recomputing after the loop is safe, because nothing inside the loop reads c_distance. Duplicate pruning matches only on person, node, edge code and edge type. The in-loop stamping was left as it is.

**Note on the Access version.** These SELECTs were ported from gQuerySelectNonkin and gQuerySelectKin. To be checked whether the VBA has the same off-by-one. If it does, it affects only edge-distance outputs, such as the edge colours in the UCINet and GUESS exports. Node distances were always correct.

## Verification

| Test | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Max distance 2, kin + non-kin (1,232 edges) | All 98 kin edges at distance 0; 80 single-kin aggregate rows blank | Kin edges have distances; aggregate labels filled in |
| Max distance 1 (7 edges) | All edges at distance 0 | All edges at distance 1 |
| Max distance 2, after NET-3 (1,232 edges, 261 people) | — | Every edge's distance equals the larger of its endpoints' node distances: 7 at distance 1, 1,225 at distance 2, 0 mismatches |

Still to check by hand in the aggregate tab: one kin tie between a pair ("K: …"), two kin ties between a pair, and one association plus one kin tie. The last two should both show "Multiple associations merged".
